column1: # 28장 말투 지시(11-10). 열: 조각 앞머리 → 지시(영어, 짧게). @scene 행은 장면 설명. "Por Martí."(todos)는 조안의 건배와 앞머리가 겹쳐 지시하지 않는다.

column2: November 11, Sant Martí, the saint's day of Montse's late brother Martí. Montse cooks fricandó, his favourite dish, for the first time since he died; Yuna cries while chopping onions, and not only because of the onions. Vale, the young Argentine lodger, arrives with alfajores and jokes that all saints are a bit Argentine. Warm, with grief underneath.
matter-of-fact, not turning round, holding back feeling; "Hoy, sí." quiet and firm

Joan, Martí's very old clockmaker friend, arrives from Sitges; Marc, the reserved locksmith, picks him up on his Vespa. Joan jokes about his late wife, then at lunch for five in Montse's kitchen he raises a toast to Martí, who "as usual is late". Affectionate, funny, a little sad.
laughing, delighted and out of breath; "Mare de Déu" in Catalan

column1: Su mujer murió hace seis años
Por eso. Si me ve desde el cielo
column2: a joke with a straight face

column1: Por Martí. Que hoy es su santo

column1: @scene 세 시 십오 분 전, 우리는 공방 지하실로
column2: Quarter to three, the workshop basement. All five go down to the restored clock, dedicated "Para S. — M. — Barcelona, 1978". Joan greets the clock like an old friend, in Catalan and then Spanish, and tells Yuna why it was stopped at ten past three: the hour her grandmother's ship left in 1978, when Martí said "Fins que torni" (Catalan for "Hasta que vuelva", until she returns). Hushed and tender.

column1: 세 시 십오 분 전, 우리는 공방 지하실로

column2: very softly, greeting the clock like an old friend; the same word in Catalan then Spanish
gently, a question he has waited to ask

column1: El barco de tu abuela salió
column2: telling it slowly, remembering; "Fins que torni" in Catalan, then "Hasta que vuelva" softly

Still in the basement. Marc reveals the clock also plays music, and he waited to hear it with Yuna. Joan says Martí built it from the one song he knew, heard one night on a hospital bench. Yuna winds the clock with her grandmother's key; the pendulum moves, and at three o'clock the clock plays her grandmother's wordless kitchen song. Montse and Yuna hum along. The emotional climax: quiet awe, tears, no big gestures.
a quiet confession; "No quería oírla sin ti" very soft
a slow smile, remembering; "esa canción me va a volver loco" fond
gentle encouragement, hand on her back

column1: Metí la llave en el primer agujero.

column2: moved, very quiet, full of wonder

column1: Cuarenta y ocho años sin cantar.

column2: Upstairs in the workshop over coffee and alfajores. Yuna tells everyone at once that she is going to Korea on the 20th to see her mother and will come back on January 8, return ticket. A tense moment while Marc is silent, then he says he will pick her up, and take her to the airport too. Relief, warmth, quiet happiness.
steady, reassuring; "Esta vez, con vuelta" with a small smile
moved, holding her face; the threat about Korea is a loving joke
softly, unsure, asking for his reaction
